examples.label: DD-PPO depth (ResNet50, Gibson 2+)
examples.title: depth DD-PPO: R > S
examples.text: Five scenes where the depth agent does better on our reconstruction than on the laser scan. The scan's floor has holes (under furniture, at windows and mirrors, along walls the scanner never saw); on S the agent is boxed in and times out, on R the floor is complete, the phantom free space is almost entirely scan-hole-filled, shortest paths get shorter (path ratio < 1) and the agent reaches the goal.

examples.label: DD-PPO RGB (SE-ResNeXt50, Gibson 2+ & MP3D)
examples.title: RGB DD-PPO: R > S
examples.text: Five scenes where the RGB agent does better on our reconstruction than on the laser scan. The RGB policy sees flat-shaded vertex colours on both worlds; a scan hole hurts it twice, as an obstacle and as a black void in its camera image, so where the scan floor is broken and ours is complete it succeeds on R. Over all scenes the RGB agent is still worse on R than on S (appearance), which the tables above report.
